preflight_dedup.reason: P020 models container inland intermodal handoffs, P021 terminal land/gate infrastructure and governance, P129 berth-side dry-bulk transfer paths, and P130 storage/reclaim. None separately models the delivered dry-bulk terminal-to-landside-carrier receipt/dispatch interface state, while generic queue, monitoring, support and degradation mechanics are already represented and must not be counted as new.

new_categories.label: terminal_dry_bulk_landside_receipt_dispatch_service_readiness
new_categories.memory: A dry-bulk terminal can have a distinct delivered landside receipt/dispatch service-state linking cargo arrival or departure opportunity to terminal operations without reducing the state to land ownership, gate infrastructure, berth equipment or storage capacity.

new_categories.label: landside_carrier_terminal_handoff_opportunity_confidence
new_categories.memory: Rail, truck or barge handoff opportunity can be represented as bounded confidence that a carrier-terminal interchange can occur, without retaining exact slots, tracks, gates, queues, schedules, rates or operating procedures.

new_categories.label: arrival_to_terminal_acceptance_interface_confidence
new_categories.memory: Inbound carrier arrival and terminal acceptance are distinct interface states: carrier presence does not by itself establish terminal acceptance readiness, and terminal readiness does not prove carrier availability.

new_categories.label: terminal_to_departing_carrier_release_interface_confidence
new_categories.memory: Outbound cargo release toward a landside carrier can be represented separately from inbound receipt and from storage/reclaim readiness, without asserting exact release documents, gate steps or dispatch sequence.

new_categories.label: landside_transfer_path_scope_confidence
new_categories.memory: Landside-interface assurance can attach to a bounded mode, handoff zone or terminal-side path scope without preserving exact tracks, roads, gates, hoppers, dumpers, loaders or route geometry.

new_categories.label: queue_access_availability_confidence
new_categories.memory: A terminal may be technically capable yet operationally constrained by access or queue availability; this can be represented qualitatively without exact queue length, appointment logic, dwell time, slot count or schedule.

new_categories.label: multi_mode_landside_interface_substitution_confidence
new_categories.memory: Where more than one landside mode or interchange path exists, substitution confidence can be modeled abstractly without claiming a specific terminal's rail, truck or barge configuration or redundancy.

new_categories.label: stockyard_feed_dispatch_boundary_confidence
new_categories.memory: The landside interface can be separated from the stockyard/storage-reclaim boundary: interface readiness may exist while feed/dispatch into storage is restricted, or vice versa.

new_categories.label: landside_interface_monitoring_indication_confidence
new_categories.memory: Monitoring or indication confidence for the landside handoff can degrade separately from the physical interface without retaining exact sensors, systems, messages, controls or displays.

new_categories.label: landside_interface_support_dependency_confidence
new_categories.memory: Power, communications, staffing, maintenance, documentation or other support dependencies can affect the delivered interface state without requiring exact dependency topology or provider identity.

new_categories.label: cargo_identity_acceptance_scope_confidence
new_categories.memory: A bounded dry-bulk handoff can depend on confidence that the cargo/lot and acceptance scope align, while exact documents, samples, specifications or custody-transfer rules remain deferred.

new_categories.label: landside_interface_degradation_restriction_isolation_restoration_lifecycle
new_categories.memory: The receipt/dispatch interface can move through available, degraded, restricted, isolated, under-restoration and restored states with scope-specific timing.

new_categories.label: multi_timestamp_landside_interface_restoration
new_categories.memory: Carrier access return, terminal acceptance or release readiness, path verification, monitoring/support recovery and restriction release can occur at different times rather than one synthetic restoration timestamp.

useful_refinements.label: dry_bulk_landside_interface_vs_container_inland_handoff
useful_refinements.memory: P020 establishes container inland intermodal/drayage/rail/barge/ICD/gate handoffs, but dry-bulk receipt/dispatch can remain a separate cargo-system interface without inheriting container-specific gate, box or inland-network semantics.

useful_refinements.label: operating_interface_vs_terminal_land_gate_infrastructure
useful_refinements.memory: P021 land/gate/yard infrastructure and concession/investment capacity do not establish the current delivered landside receipt/dispatch handoff service-state.

useful_refinements.label: landside_interface_vs_berth_transfer_path
useful_refinements.memory: P129 berth-side shiploader/unloader/conveyor path readiness does not establish rail/truck/barge receipt or dispatch availability on the landside boundary.

useful_refinements.label: receipt_dispatch_interface_vs_storage_reclaim
useful_refinements.memory: P130 storage/reclaim service can be available while the landside handoff is restricted, and landside receipt/dispatch can be available while stockyard feed/reclaim is constrained.

duplicates.label: generic_queue_monitoring_support_and_service_lifecycle
duplicates.memory: Generic availability, queue/access confidence, monitoring, support dependency, degradation, restriction, isolation and restoration mechanics repeat prior inland, terminal and service-state families.

duplicates.label: generic_downstream_effect_does_not_prove_root_cause
duplicates.memory: Stockyard restriction, berth readiness loss, throughput uncertainty, rehandling, vessel waiting or schedule effects do not by themselves prove a carrier, queue, handoff or transfer-path root cause; this causal boundary is already campaign-wide.

stop_reason: The bounded dry-bulk landside receipt/dispatch interface questions are answered at structural Memory level. Further recall trends toward exact gates, tracks, hoppers, queues, rates, capacities, schedules, documents, controls, procedures, providers or incidents that require Evidence or a different explicitly selected frontier.
epistemic_boundary: Memory-only defensive dry-bulk terminal landside receipt/dispatch interface orientation and source-discovery output; not rail, trucking, barge, terminal-operation, queue-management, maintenance, troubleshooting or emergency guidance and not proof of any exact layout, queue, capacity, rate, schedule, document, procedure, provider, incident or current-readiness fact.
